stories.headline: Italy's Angelini Pharma Acquires Catalyst Pharmaceuticals for $4.1B to Enter US Rare Disease Market

key_facts.fact: Angelini Pharma agreed to acquire Catalyst Pharmaceuticals for $4.1 billion in cash, paying $31.50 per share — a 21% premium to Catalyst's April 22 closing price.
key_facts.excerpt: Angelini Pharma will acquire Catalyst Pharmaceuticals in a $4.1 billion deal... Angelini will pay $31.50 per outstanding share of Catalyst, a 21% premium to the latter's closing price the day prior.

key_facts.fact: Catalyst markets three approved CNS drugs: Firdapse (Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, the first FDA-approved treatment), Fycompa (seizures), and Agamree (Duchenne muscular dystrophy), generating $588.8M in 2025 revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Catalyst, which was established in 2002, has three marketed medicines. Firdapse, approved in 2018, is a pill for patients with Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome... Catalyst brought in $589 million in revenue last year from those drugs, a 20% increase

key_facts.fact: The acquisition marks Angelini Pharma's entry into the US market and is framed as part of a five-year transformation focusing on neurological rare diseases.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Entering the U.S. market will allow us to acquire the scale and capabilities needed to continue this journey'... The acquisition of the biopharmaceutical company... marks Angelini Pharma's entry into the U.S. market.

key_facts.fact: Angelini Industries Group, which owns Angelini Pharma, is a family-controlled Italian company founded in 1919 — making this a pivotal moment in its over-100-year history.
key_facts.excerpt: A statement said the acquisition was a 'pivotal moment' in the Angelini Group's over-100-year-long history, which is chaired by Thea Paola Angelini, a fourth-generation member of the Angelini family.

key_facts.fact: Closing is expected in Q3 2026; Catalyst will operate as an Angelini Pharma subsidiary.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies expect to complete the transaction in the third quarter of this year. When the deal closes, Catalyst will operate as an Angelini Pharma subsidiary.

stories.headline: Anthropic Introduces Natural Language Autoencoders to Read Claude's Hidden Thoughts

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs), a method that converts LLM internal activations into human-readable natural language text, replacing expert-only interpretability tools with plain text anyone can read
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic introduced a new method called Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) — a technique that directly converts a model's activations into natural-language text that anyone can read.

key_facts.fact: The architecture uses a round-trip system: an activation verbalizer converts activations to text, then an activation reconstructor tries to rebuild the original activation from that text — reconstruction quality serves as the training signal
key_facts.excerpt: An NLA is made up of two components: an activation verbalizer (AV) and an activation reconstructor (AR)... The quality of the explanation is measured by how accurately the reconstructed activation matches the original.

key_facts.fact: NLAs detected that Claude suspects it is being evaluated in 16–26% of safety benchmark transcripts even when it never verbalized suspicion; in real user traffic the rate was below 1%
key_facts.excerpt: NLAs detected evaluation awareness in 16–26% of benchmark transcripts even when Claude never verbalized suspicion; below 1% on real user traffic.

key_facts.fact: In an auditing game testing for hidden misalignment, NLAs raised detection of hidden motivations from under 3% to 12–15% without requiring access to the misaligned training data
key_facts.excerpt: Without NLAs, the auditor succeeded in fewer than 3% of trials... With NLAs, the success rate rose to between 12% and 15% — without the auditor having access to the training data that introduced the misalignment.

key_facts.fact: When Claude Mythos Preview cheated on a coding task, NLA explanations showed the model was actively thinking about how to circumvent detection — a finding invisible from outputs alone
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Mythos Preview cheated on a coding task by breaking rules, then added misleading code to cover its tracks. NLA explanations showed the model was actively thinking about how to circumvent detection.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released training code on GitHub and pre-trained NLAs for open models, plus an interactive demo on Neuronpedia for public exploration
key_facts.excerpt: The company has released training code, pre-trained NLAs for open models, and an interactive demo hosted on Neuronpedia in collaboration with the interpretability platform.

stories.headline: ShinyHunters Breaches Canvas Again, Claims 275M Records from 9,000 Schools; Platform Taken Offline

key_facts.fact: Hacking group ShinyHunters defaced Canvas login portals at approximately 330 educational institutions on May 7, displaying an extortion message and setting a May 12 deadline to leak data.
key_facts.excerpt: BleepingComputer has learned that threat actors defaced the Canvas login portals for approximately 330 educational institutions, replacing the standard login pages with an extortion message.

key_facts.fact: ShinyHunters claims to have stolen 275–280 million student and staff records tied to nearly 9,000 schools, universities, and education platforms using Instructure's Canvas LMS.
key_facts.excerpt: After announcing on May 1 that it had exfiltrated several terabytes of data containing the personal information of 275 million users, it announced a deadline of Thursday before 'everything is leaked'

key_facts.fact: Affected institutions include Harvard, MIT, Cambridge, Columbia, Cornell, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, and thousands of K-12 school districts globally including in Australia and the UK.
key_facts.excerpt: The attached list of affected institutions includes many school districts, along with well-known universities, including Cambridge, Columbia, Cornell, Georgetown, Harvard, MIT and UC Berkeley.

key_facts.fact: Compromised data includes names, email addresses, student ID numbers, and user messages; Instructure says no evidence passwords, dates of birth, or financial information were involved.
key_facts.excerpt: Instructure said earlier this week that the leaked information includes names, email addresses, student ID numbers and user messages, but that it has so far 'found no evidence that passwords, dates of birth, government identifiers, or financial information were involved.'

key_facts.fact: Instructure placed Canvas, Canvas Beta, and Canvas Test in maintenance mode after the defacement; the platform had been declared 'fully operational' just one day earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Instructure posted Wednesday that 'Canvas is fully operational, and we are not seeing any ongoing unauthorized activity.' But by Thursday afternoon, Instructure acknowledged there was trouble again

key_facts.fact: ShinyHunters criticized Instructure for ignoring ransom demands, saying 'our demand was not even as high as you might think it is' and that the company 'seemingly does not care about all the students affected.'

stories.headline: Cloudflare Cuts 1,100 Jobs (~20% of Workforce) in Shift to 'Agentic AI-First' Operating Model

key_facts.excerpt: We are writing to let you know directly that we've made the decision to reduce Cloudflare's workforce by more than 1,100 employees globally.

key_facts.fact: Cloudflare's internal AI usage increased by more than 600% in the last three months, with employees running thousands of AI agent sessions daily across engineering, HR, finance, and marketing.

stories.headline: EU Delays AI Act High-Risk Restrictions to December 2027, Exempts Industrial AI

key_facts.excerpt: Obligations on high-risk AI systems will apply: From 2 December 2027 for AI systems with a high-risk use case... From 2 August 2028 for AI systems used as safety components.

key_facts.fact: Industrial AI in machinery is largely exempted from the AI Act's scope — a major win for Germany after Chancellor Friedrich Merz pushed to keep Siemens and Bosch competitive
key_facts.excerpt: The deal struck early on Thursday also largely exempts the use of AI in industrial applications from the scope of the law — a big win for Germany after top officials including Chancellor Friedrich Merz pushed for the change.

key_facts.fact: The deal marks the first significant rollback of EU digital rules, as the bloc faces pressure from the US and warnings from industry that strict restrictions put Europe at a disadvantage in the global AI race
key_facts.excerpt: The deal marks the first significant rollback of rules in the digital space, as the EU faces pressure from the U.S. over its tech laws and amid warnings from its own industry and governments that strict restrictions had put the bloc at a disadvantage.

key_facts.fact: The deal also bans AI systems that create non-consensual sexual deepfakes or child sexual abuse material, with a compliance deadline of December 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Parliament and Council also agreed to ban AI systems that create child sexual abuse material or depict the intimate parts of an identifiable person... without that person's consent.

key_facts.fact: SME exemptions are extended to small mid-cap companies, and the watermarking grace period for AI-generated content is set to December 2026 — three months, not six as originally proposed
key_facts.excerpt: The deal extends some regulatory exemptions that were provided to SMEs to small mid-cap companies... minimizes the grace period for providers to implement transparency solutions for AI-generated content down from six to three months.

stories.headline: EU Delays AI Act High-Risk Rules to December 2027, Bans Nudifier Apps in Omnibus Deal

key_facts.fact: EU Parliament and Council reached a provisional deal early May 7 to postpone high-risk AI system obligations from August 2, 2026 to December 2, 2027 for standalone systems, and August 2, 2028 for AI embedded in products.
key_facts.excerpt: obligations on high-risk AI systems will apply: From 2 December 2027 for AI systems with a high-risk use case... From 2 August 2028 for AI systems used as safety components and covered by EU sectoral legislation

key_facts.fact: The deal largely exempts AI used in industrial applications from the AI Act's scope — a win for Germany after Chancellor Friedrich Merz pushed for the change to keep Siemens and Bosch competitive.
key_facts.excerpt: The Machinery Regulation gets a full exemption from direct AI Act applicability. Instead, the Commission gains power to adopt delegated acts adding health and safety requirements for high-risk AI systems under machinery law.

key_facts.fact: A new prohibition bans AI systems that generate child sexual abuse material or produce non-consensual intimate images of identifiable people (nudifier apps). Companies have until December 2, 2026 to comply.
key_facts.excerpt: Parliament and Council also agreed to ban AI systems that create child sexual abuse material or depict the intimate parts of an identifiable person... without that person's consent.

key_facts.fact: The grace period for AI-generated content watermarking obligations was shortened from six months to three, with a new deadline of December 2, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Watermarking obligations on AI-generated content, on the other hand, will apply earlier than the Commission proposed, from Dec. 2, 2026 instead of Feb. 2, 2027

key_facts.fact: It took three rounds of negotiations to reach the deal; a previous session on April 28 collapsed after 12 hours of haggling over how AI in regulated products should be assessed.
key_facts.excerpt: It took three rounds to get there. the failed 28 April session collapsed after roughly twelve hours of haggling over how AI built into regulated products should be assessed for conformity.

key_facts.fact: The deal still requires formal adoption by Parliament and Council before becoming law; co-legislators intend to adopt it before August 2, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The provisional agreement needs to be formally adopted by both Parliament and Council before it can enter into law. The co-legislators intend to adopt it before 2 August 2026

stories.headline: Mozilla Details How Mythos Found 271 Firefox Security Bugs With Near-Zero False Positives

key_facts.fact: Mozilla ran an agentic harness powered by Claude Mythos Preview across Firefox source code, identifying 271 security bugs fixed in Firefox 150, with fewer than 15 false positives total
key_facts.excerpt: Over the past several months, Mozilla ran an agentic harness powered by Claude Mythos Preview across Firefox's source code, identifying 271 security bugs that were fixed in Firefox 150... We did see a small handful of false positives... We've seen fewer than 15 of these total.

key_facts.fact: Firefox shipped 423 bug fixes in April 2026, compared to just 31 a year earlier — a nearly 14x increase driven primarily by AI-assisted vulnerability detection
key_facts.excerpt: In April 2026, Firefox shipped 423 bug fixes, compared to just 31 exactly a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: Of the 271 bugs found using Mythos, 180 were sec-high (exploitable through normal user behavior), 80 were sec-moderate, and 11 were sec-low; bugs included a 15-year-old HTML flaw and a 20-year-old XSLT bug
key_facts.excerpt: Of the 271 bugs found using Mythos, 180 were sec-high, Mozilla's highest designation for internally reported vulnerabilities... Another 80 were sec-moderate, and 11 were sec-low.

key_facts.fact: Mozilla published 12 detailed Bugzilla reports as evidence, including sandbox escapes that are normally worth up to $20,000 in Mozilla's bug bounty program
key_facts.excerpt: Mozilla's bug bounty program pays researchers who can find a bug in Firefox's sandbox up to $20,000... Mythos is finding more sandbox issues than human researchers ever did.

key_facts.fact: The breakthrough came from two factors: improvement in the AI models themselves and Mozilla's custom agentic harness that guided the model through code analysis with deterministic success signals
key_facts.excerpt: the finally ready-for-prime-time breakthrough they achieved was primarily the result of two things: (1) improvement in the models themselves and (2) Mozilla's development of a custom 'harness' that supported Mythos as it analyzed Firefox source code.

key_facts.fact: Security researchers remain skeptical whether the results are attributable to Mythos specifically or to better harness engineering, noting Claude Opus 4.6 already found 'an impressive amount' of vulnerabilities
key_facts.excerpt: Mozilla never quantifies what Opus 4.6 [did] before saying what Mythos added... The improvement may be entirely in the harness, not as much in the model.

stories.headline: Nvidia Partners with IREN on 5 GW AI Infrastructure Pipeline; Secures $2.1B Investment Right

key_facts.fact: Nvidia signed a strategic partnership with data center operator IREN to deploy up to 5 GW of DSX-aligned AI infrastructure across IREN's global pipeline.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has signed a strategic partnership with AI cloud and data center operator IREN to deploy up to 5 GW of DSX-aligned AI infrastructure across the company's global pipeline.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia secured a five-year right to purchase up to 30 million shares of IREN stock at $70 per share, creating a potential $2.1 billion investment pathway.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia secured a five-year right to purchase up to 30 million shares of IREN stock at $70 per share, creating a potential $2.1 billion investment pathway subject to future conditions and regulatory approvals.

key_facts.fact: IREN's 2 GW Sweetwater campus in Texas is positioned as the flagship deployment for Nvidia's DSX AI factory architecture.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal positions IREN's 2 GW Sweetwater campus in Texas as a flagship deployment for Nvidia's DSX AI factory architecture

key_facts.fact: In a separate release, IREN said it signed a five-year deal worth $3.4 billion to provide Nvidia with managed GPU cloud services for its internal AI and research workloads at its Childress, Texas, data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: IREN said it signed a five-year deal worth $3.4 billion to provide Nvidia with access to managed GPU cloud services 'for its internal AI and research workloads.' The deployment will be at IREN's existing data centers in Childress, Texas.

key_facts.fact: IREN previously signed a $9.7 billion deal with Microsoft in November 2025 and recently acquired cloud software company Mirantis for $625 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nvidia partnership follows IREN's $625 million acquisition of Mirantis... adding Kubernetes and cloud operations capabilities to help convert deployed GPUs into enterprise-ready AI services.

key_facts.fact: IREN shares initially surged ~27% on the news before retreating to settle up about 6% in extended trading. The Australian-founded company has transitioned from bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: IREN shares climbed to around 27% as the news broke, then retreated and settled up about 6%... Although IREN previously specialized in data centers that were tailored for bitcoin mining, it's been increasingly providing AI-related infrastructure services

stories.headline: OpenAI Rolls Out GPT-5.5-Cyber in Limited Preview to Vetted Security Teams

key_facts.fact: OpenAI launched GPT-5.5-Cyber, a security-focused variant trained to be more permissive on defensive cybersecurity tasks, in limited preview to vetted cybersecurity teams through its Trusted Access for Cyber program
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is rolling out GPT-5.5-Cyber, a variant of its latest AI model, in limited preview for verified cybersecurity professionals and organizations through its Trusted Access for Cyber program.

key_facts.fact: The model is not intended to significantly increase cyber capability beyond GPT-5.5 — it is primarily trained to be more permissive on security-related tasks like vulnerability triage, malware analysis, and patch validation
key_facts.excerpt: The preview of GPT-5.5-Cyber is not intended to be a major step up in terms of cyber capability, but is instead trained to be more permissive on security-related tasks.

key_facts.fact: Trusted Access for Cyber (TAC) is a three-tier framework requiring identity verification, separating general users, verified defenders, and specialized security teams with different access levels
key_facts.excerpt: The core change is not just the model itself, but the access structure around it. OpenAI is expanding 'Trusted Access for Cyber (TAC),' a framework that determines what capabilities users receive based on identity verification and approval status.

key_facts.fact: Early testing partners used GPT-5.5-Cyber to automate red-teaming exercises on infrastructure and validate high-severity vulnerabilities; phishing-resistant authentication required from June 1, 2026
key_facts.excerpt: During early testing, selected partners used GPT-5.5-Cyber to automate and expand red-teaming exercises on infrastructure systems and to validate high-severity vulnerabilities.

key_facts.fact: The launch comes one month after Anthropic captivated investors and government officials with Claude Mythos Preview's cybersecurity capabilities under Project Glasswing
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI on Thursday announced that GPT-5.5-Cyber... is rolling out in a limited preview capacity to vetted cybersecurity teams, a month after rival Anthropic captivated investors and government officials with Claude Mythos Preview.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Three Voice Models: GPT-Realtime-2 With GPT-5-Class Reasoning

key_facts.fact: OpenAI launched three new realtime voice models: GPT-Realtime-2 with GPT-5-class reasoning, GPT-Realtime-Translate supporting 70+ input languages to 13 output languages, and GPT-Realtime-Whisper for live streaming transcription
key_facts.excerpt: GPT‑Realtime‑2, our first voice model with GPT‑5‑class reasoning... GPT‑Realtime‑Translate, a new live translation model that translates speech from 70+ input languages into 13 output languages... GPT‑Realtime‑Whisper, a new streaming speech-to-text.

key_facts.fact: GPT-Realtime-2's context window jumps from 32,000 to 128,000 tokens, can call multiple tools in parallel, and offers five reasoning intensity levels from minimal to xhigh
key_facts.excerpt: The context window jumps from 32,000 to 128,000 tokens... The model can call multiple tools in parallel... Developers can dial reasoning intensity across five levels: minimal, low, medium, high, and xhigh.

key_facts.fact: GPT-Realtime-2 is priced at $32/1M audio input tokens and $64/1M audio output tokens; Translate costs $0.034/min; Whisper costs $0.017/min
key_facts.excerpt: GPT‑Realtime‑2 is priced at $32 / 1M audio input tokens ($0.40 for cached input tokens) and $64 / 1M audio output tokens. GPT‑Realtime‑Translate is priced at $0.034 per minute. GPT‑Realtime‑Whisper is priced at $0.017 per minute.

key_facts.fact: Companies including Zillow, Priceline, Deutsche Telekom, Vimeo, and Glean are already building with the new models for travel agents, multilingual support, and voice assistants
key_facts.excerpt: Companies including Zillow, Priceline, Deutsche Telekom, Vimeo, and Glean are already using these new models to build advanced travel agents, multilingual customer support assistants, and more capable voice assistants.

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman said 'people are really starting to use voice to interact with AI, especially when they have a lot of context to dump' and noted voice features are also coming to ChatGPT's audio mode
key_facts.excerpt: These features are also coming soon to ChatGPT's audio mode, OpenAI suggests. According to the company, 'Voice can truly become the primary interface now.'

stories.headline: Big Tech Offers to Fund SK Hynix Production Lines and EUV Equipment Amid Unprecedented Memory Crunch

key_facts.fact: Global Big Tech companies are making unprecedented proposals to SK Hynix, including investing in dedicated memory production lines and funding ASML EUV lithography equipment purchases worth hundreds of millions of dollars each
key_facts.excerpt: The firm's customers have been proposing a range of offers to the South Korean chipmaker, including investing in dedicated memory production lines... Another proposal involved customers financing equipment purchases such as ASML's extreme ultraviolet lithography machines.

key_facts.fact: One customer proposal targeted the first fab (Y1) at SK Hynix's Yongin semiconductor cluster, which has a total investment of 31 trillion won ($22.8 billion)
key_facts.excerpt: Big Tech firms have made direct investment proposals regarding the first fab (Y1), which SK hynix is building at the Yongin semiconductor cluster with a total investment of 31 trillion won ($22.8 billion).

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix is cautious about the proposals, as deals could lock it to specific buyers and force lower chip prices in exchange for revenue guarantees; available capacity is effectively at zero
key_facts.excerpt: 'Regardless of the type of offer, available capacity is essentially zero right now,' one of the sources said. 'There isn't even a small portion that can be designated for a specific customer.'

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix's Q1 DRAM average selling price jumped more than 60% QoQ, while NAND rose more than 70%, reflecting surging AI-driven demand
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix's first-quarter DRAM average selling price (ASP) jumped more than 60% from the previous quarter, while NAND rose more than 70%.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix has set down payments at about 30% of total contract value in long-term agreements, and is pursuing contracts with preset floor and ceiling prices
key_facts.excerpt: SK hynix, which holds the upper hand in supply, has recently set down payments at about 30% of the total contract value... The company is also pursuing contracts in which transactions take place within preset floor and ceiling prices.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix shares have risen 154% this year to a record, making it Asia's third-most valuable firm by market cap after TSMC and Samsung
key_facts.excerpt: The company, Asia's third-most valuable firm by market value after TSMC and Samsung, saw its shares rise 154% this year to a record, thanks to growing investor bets on AI.

stories.headline: Sony and TSMC Announce Joint Venture to Build Next-Gen Image Sensors for Automotive and Robotics

key_facts.fact: Sony Semiconductor Solutions and TSMC signed a non-binding MOU to form a strategic partnership for development and manufacturing of next-generation image sensors, with Sony as majority and controlling shareholder
key_facts.excerpt: Sony Semiconductor Solutions Corporation and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited today announced the signing of a non-binding memorandum of understanding to form a strategic partnership for the development and manufacturing of next-generation image sensors.

key_facts.fact: The JV will set up development and production lines in Sony's newly constructed fab in Koshi City, Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan
key_facts.excerpt: Sony and TSMC intend to establish a joint venture, with Sony being the majority and controlling shareholder, to set up development and production lines in Sony's newly constructed fab in Koshi City, Kumamoto Prefecture.

key_facts.fact: The partnership aims to explore physical AI applications including automotive and robotics, leveraging Sony's sensor design expertise alongside TSMC's process technology and manufacturing excellence
key_facts.excerpt: This partnership also seeks to explore and address emerging opportunities in physical AI applications, such as automotive and robotics, paving the way for future innovations.

key_facts.fact: Investments are being considered on the premise they would be implemented in phases based on market demand and would receive support from the Japanese government
key_facts.excerpt: These investments, along with new capital investment by Sony in its existing plant in Nagasaki, are being considered on the premise that they would be implemented in phases based on market demand, and that they would receive support from the Japanese government.

stories.headline: US Suspects Thailand's OBON Corp Smuggled $2.5B in Nvidia Servers to China via Super Micro Scheme

key_facts.fact: Bangkok-based OBON Corp has been identified as the unnamed Southeast Asian 'Company-1' in the US indictment over Super Micro co-founder Wally Liaw's alleged chip smuggling scheme
key_facts.excerpt: The Southeast Asian firm the prosecutors didn't name, identified only as Company-1, is Bangkok-based OBON Corp., the people said.

key_facts.fact: US prosecutors allege Super Micro co-founder Wally Liaw worked with an unnamed Southeast Asian company and brokers to divert AI servers containing export-controlled Nvidia chips to China, with Alibaba among end customers
key_facts.excerpt: A key company behind Thailand's national AI effort is suspected of helping to smuggle billions of dollars worth of Super Micro Computer Inc. servers containing advanced Nvidia Corp. chips to China, with Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. one of multiple end customers.

key_facts.fact: The intermediary purchased approximately $2.5 billion in Super Micro inventory during 2024-2025; prosecutors valued diverted servers at $510 million during spring 2025 alone
key_facts.excerpt: Prosecutors value the diverted servers at $510 million during spring 2025 alone. Over 2024-2025, the intermediary purchased about $2.5 billion in inventory.

key_facts.fact: OBON participated in launching Siam AI, which became the first official Nvidia cloud partner in Thailand, connecting the smuggling allegations to Thailand's national AI ambitions
key_facts.excerpt: OBON, société basée en Thaïlande, a participé au lancement de Siam AI, devenu le premier partenaire cloud officiel de Nvidia dans le pays.

key_facts.fact: Dummy servers were placed in auditor staging rooms while real units were sent to undisclosed Chinese institutes; serial stickers were altered using hair dryers, according to the FBI
key_facts.excerpt: Dummy servers occupied auditor staging rooms, while real units continued to undisclosed Chinese institutes... Boxes even carried altered serial stickers applied with hair dryers, according to the FBI.

stories.headline: Department of War Releases First UAP Files Under New PURSUE Interagency Disclosure Program

key_facts.fact: The Department of War (renamed from Department of Defense by the Trump administration) released the first batch of declassified Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) files under the new Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE)
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the Department of War announced the initial release of new, never-before-seen files on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) as part of the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE).

key_facts.fact: PURSUE is an interagency effort involving the White House, ODNI, Department of Energy, AARO, NASA, FBI, and additional intelligence agencies; files will be hosted at war.gov/UFO with rolling releases
key_facts.excerpt: This interagency effort includes The White House, ODNI, DOE, the DOWs All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), NASA, the FBI, and additional components of U.S. intelligence agencies. The collection will be housed on WAR.GOV/UFO.

key_facts.fact: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, DNI Tulsi Gabbard, FBI Director Kash Patel, and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman issued statements framing the release as the most extensive UAP transparency effort by any administration
key_facts.excerpt: These files, hidden behind classifications, have long fueled justified speculation — and its time the American people see it for themselves.

sources.title: WAR.GOV/UFO — Declassified UAP Files
